name: Saudi Arabia
headline: Saudi Arabia: +4.6% growth in 2025, 2.0% inflation, debt 32% of GDP
sections: Saudi Arabia is a $1.27 trillion economy (2025), the world's 20th-largest of 215 measured. Real output grew +4.6% in 2025, faster than the world median of +3.5%. Income per person is $74K at purchasing-power parity (2025), against a world median of $21K. Manufacturing accounts for 15.8% of GDP (2025).
Consumer prices rose 2.0% in 2025, broadly within typical target ranges. Unemployment stood at 3.2% (2025), below the world median of 5.1%. Youth unemployment was 10.0% (2025).
Gross government debt is 32% of GDP (2025), a low level. The general government balance is −5.8% of GDP (2025), a deficit beyond the common 3% benchmark.
The current account balance is −2.6% of GDP (2025). Trade equals 58% of GDP (2025), a fairly open economy. Net FDI inflows were 2.6% of GDP (2025).
IMF projections put government debt at 49% of GDP by 2031, still rising from today's level. Life expectancy is 79.0 years (2024). Population: 36.0 million (2025).
note: Built from official World Bank and IMF data; IMF projections are labelled as projections.
